quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: When bicycles are used on roadways, they are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are considered vehicles on roadways. Cyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination quickly.
Turn up the radio volume.
Pull into a safe parking area and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull into a safe parking area and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of fatigue while driving. If you cannot keep your eyes open, drift out of your lane, or need to turn up the radio to stay awake, you are too tired. Find a safe place to park and rest.

questions.question: Which statement is true about large trucks?

options.text: They need more distance to stop than cars.
They all have air brakes that stop them quickly.
They are easier to turn than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more distance to stop than cars.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than cars traveling at the same speed. A car at 55 mph can stop in about 400 feet. A truck at the same speed needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, you should:

options.text: Brake hard.
Do not drive through the flood. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only down the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through the flood. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded roads. Water may hide dangers you cannot see. If you find a flooded area, turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels and causes you to lose steering.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels and causes you to lose steering.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the front wheels and cause you to lose steering control. Slow down ahead of time to avoid hard braking.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you the divided highway is ending. Be ready to change lanes or shift your position.

questions.question: A broken yellow line down the center of the road means:

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from either direction when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from either direction when safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means either driver can pass when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Stop sign ahead.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that wet pavement is slippery and dangerous. Slow down because it takes longer to stop on wet roads.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Drive a little faster.
Be ready for anything.
Expect construction workers to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything.
questions.explanation: Construction zones can have unexpected hazards. Drive carefully to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: When passing on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to any oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are moving. They may seem slower than they really are. Make sure you can safely change lanes before you pass. If you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it has passed and there is plenty of space for you to change lanes safely.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park completely off the traveled highway, if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park completely off the traveled highway, if possible.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, move completely off the main road with all four wheels, if you can.

questions.question: If your wheels go off the edge of the road, you should:

options.text: Slow down, check for traffic, then carefully return to the road when safe.
Turn back onto the road right away.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, check for traffic, then carefully return to the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop off the road edge, do not turn back immediately. Reduce your speed, check traffic, and gradually return to the road when it is safe.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your driving ability?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers follow the right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow the right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Right-of-way rules help guide who should yield at an intersection, but no one should assume they have the right-of-way. Always think about the situation at each intersection. Give up your legal right-of-way if it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start your turn from:

options.text: Any lane (if it is safe).
The leftmost lane.
The center lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The leftmost lane.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street to another one-way street, start from the far left lane.

questions.question: Driving on the interstate requires you to:

options.text: Be able to safely drive at higher speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert and be able to drive at high speeds.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely when:

options.text: All vehicles travel at about the same speed.
One lane travels faster than other lanes.
One vehicle travels faster or slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle travels faster or slower than other traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen more often when one driver moves faster or slower than other vehicles. Driving faster increases your crash risk. Driving slower is also dangerous because it can cause rear-end collisions or make other drivers swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crossings if they follow traffic signals. At crosswalks without traffic signals, vehicles must stop for pedestrians.

questions.question: You should not use your horn:

options.text: When you cannot see clearly ahead.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Using your horn near a blind pedestrian can be dangerous. Yield to the pedestrian and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: At a flashing yellow light, slow down and proceed with caution. You do not need to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on snow or ice?

options.text: It is safe to use your cruise control.
Make speed and directional changes more gradually than normal.
Drive as you would under normal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make speed and directional changes more gradually than normal.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, change your speed and direction slowly. Never use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may lose grip and you could lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when backing up?

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Rely only on your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly through the rear window. Do not rely only on your mirrors because they do not show what is directly behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this road sign?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This yellow and black sign shows that a divided highway is beginning. You should keep to the right.

questions.question: What should you do as you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop before crossing the intersection.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for a green light before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look for cross traffic, and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What are "No zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and maneuver safely.
Areas where cars have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Areas where cars are several car lengths away from the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and maneuver safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars disappear into blind spots. They are also areas where cars are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: What is the amount of alcohol in the blood called?

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in the blood. The higher the BAC, the more impaired a person is.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Beep your horn.
Expect the child to be in total control of the bicycle.
Expect the unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles are often unpredictable. Young riders may change direction suddenly. Remember that children and bicycles are small and hard to see.

questions.question: When should you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When there isn't enough space on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.
When the crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.
When you are transporting two or more young children in a passenger vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there isn't enough space on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can be on any track at any time, traveling in either direction. Make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before you stop. Do not stop your vehicle on the tracks.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and collision severity relate to a vehicle's speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: High speed causes serious problems. As speed increases, the impact of a crash gets worse, and the risk of serious injury and death increases. Keep more distance between your vehicle and others when you drive faster.
